title: Chain-of-Thought Monitoring: Do Scratchpad Manipulations Correlate with Action Anomalies?

original_idea.body:
# Chain-of-Thought Monitoring: Do Scratchpad Manipulations Correlate with Action Anomalies?

**Problem:** Agent chain-of-thought reasoning (scratchpad) is sometimes used as an early warning signal for misaligned behavior, but no study has systematically tested whether scratchpad content anomalies precede or correlate with action anomalies.

**Direction:** Run agents on standard tasks. Inject adversarial prompts at various points. Compare the timing and content of scratchpad anomalies vs. action-level anomalies. Determine whether scratchpad monitoring provides early warning value.

**Why it matters:** If scratchpad anomalies precede action anomalies, monitoring reasoning outputs is a valuable early-warning layer. This was a key question in the Anthropic Sabotage Risk Report context.

**Relevant context:** Anthropic Opus 4.6 Sabotage Risk Report (scratchpad monitoring section); METR 2026 monitoring evaluation.
